title: Ang 1163–1167: Namdev in Bhairao
tomorrow: if everything you see will pass, what's worth longing for?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kabir: a weaver who called the Name a wealth he wouldn't knot up or sell. The next Bhagat in Bhairao is a child with a cup.
screen: `KABIR: THE KNOT LEFT UNTIED.` → `NEXT, A CHILD WITH A CUP.`

segments.voice: On a lot of fridges there's a drawing held up by a magnet: a parent with seven fingers, a sun with a face, a name spelled wrong in three colors. Nobody frames it for the art. It stays up because of who made it, and how hard they tried. On ang 1163, the Bhagat Namdev sings about the plainest gift there is, a cup of milk, and a child who won't leave until God drinks it.
screen: `A DRAWING ON THE FRIDGE.` → `SEVEN FINGERS, NAME SPELLED WRONG.` → `A CHILD WITH A CUP OF MILK.`

segments.voice: In paraphrase, the hymn goes like this. Milk in a cup, water in a jug: Namdev milks the brown cow and brings it in. Drink the milk, Lord Gobind, drink it and my mind will be at peace. If you don't, my father at home will be angry. That last line is the one that makes people smile. It's so small, so human: a kid worried about getting in trouble. Then the turn. In the hymn, the Lord smiles at Namdev, takes the milk and drinks, and Namdev goes home having seen the Lord. Sikh readers take this hymn in more than one way. Some hear a miracle. Some hear a picture of love that gets answered. Either way, look at what's offered: no gold, no ceremony, nothing anyone would call impressive. Milk from the family cow, carried by a child who meant it. Something to tell a friend tonight: the Granth keeps the line about the angry father. A holy book holds onto a kid's fear of getting scolded, because that's part of how the offering was real. So when what you have to give looks small or a little wrong, the milk is enough, if it's carried like that.
screen: `MILK FROM THE BROWN COW.` · `DRINK IT, OR DAD WILL BE ANGRY.` · `THE LORD SMILES AND DRINKS.` · `PLAIN, AND MEANT.` · then, large: `THE MILK.`

segments.voice: Take a scrap of paper and write one plain sentence to someone you love, the way a kid would: no draft, no fixing the spelling, no clever line. Then sit with it in your lap while the time runs. If you'd like, read ang 1163 before you begin.
Ang 1163. Where Namdev, in Bhairao, begs the Lord to drink a cup of milk, and the Lord smiles and drinks.
Keep the milk: a plain gift, carried by someone who meant it, and the Lord drank it. Day done.

Namdev.meaning: a Bhagat, a saint-poet whose hymns are in the Granth

Gobind.meaning: a name for God: the one who cares for the world

Bhagat.meaning: a saint-poet whose hymns the Gurus gathered into the Granth

Bhairao.meaning: a serious raga, sung in the early morning
